items.summary:
Belgian authorities have ordered Google to stop construction on a large datacentre in southern Wallonia because the company's requests to modify its original planning permission had not been approved. Raphaël Stokis, a Wallonia regional official speaking to RTBF, said inspectors found the building nearly finished with structural work complete even though the permit had been refused, and that 300 workers were given a verbal order to stop work later confirmed in writing.

Google stated it remained committed to an open dialogue with the regional authorities. The company's 2025 application sought to merge two planned datacentres into one larger facility and switch from air cooling to liquid cooling by drawing water from the nearby Sambre River, a change initially approved in April but revoked in August over drought concerns after residents and protest groups appealed; Google has now appealed that decision. The building occupies about 3 hectares (7.4 acres) of a 50-hectare business park on a former coalmine at Aiseau-Presles, roughly 15km west of Charleroi, and is one of three originally planned for the site.

Nicolas Yernaux, a regional government spokesperson speaking to Agence France-Presse, said a report was being submitted to public prosecutors alleging illegal construction covering about 3 hectares. Greenpeace published drone footage showing ongoing work despite the revoked permit and filed an emergency appeal, arguing that energy-intensive datacentres cannot be allowed to proceed amid intensifying climate concerns in the region.

A ruling on Google's appeal is expected on 7 January. The dispute joins other legal challenges facing tech companies building datacentres for AI demand across Europe; in October Finland opened a criminal investigation into possible environmental law breaches at a planned Google site, with work halted pending assessments.
items.title: Google Ordered to Halt Belgium Datacentre Construction Over Missing Permit

items.summary: An international agency, S&P Global Ratings, upgraded Sri Lanka's credit rating to B- on November 27, marking its first change in more than a year as the country continues its economic recovery. The upgrade raised both the foreign currency and local currency sovereign ratings from CCC+ to B-, with a stable outlook, reflecting efforts to strengthen fiscal and external buffers since the 2022 crisis when Sri Lanka defaulted on US$46 billion (S$59.31 billion) in external debt.
items.title: Sri Lanka Credit Rating Upgraded to B-

items.summary:
Used Tesla Cybertruck prices rose sharply after Elon Musk announced the end of production at Giga Texas. CarGurus' price index put the average used Cybertruck at $89,715, up 9.84% over the last 30 days and 13.5% over 90 days, while Visor reported a like-for-like increase of +15% versus last month with an average asking price of $101,784 across 171 used trucks.

The gains track Tesla's own moves: Musk announced the production winddown on November 6 and raised prices by up to 10% that day, followed a week later by stopping sales of every Cybertruck except the Cyberbeast at $109,990, with another bump this week to $114,990. CarGurus' chart shows the average price flat near $80,000 from July through late October before bending upward in November.

Dealers are pushing prices much higher still; one New Jersey dealer now asks $150,790 for a used Cyberbeast with 4,493 miles, roughly $36,000 above Tesla's new-vehicle price. CarGurus flags that listing as overpriced by $35,773 and notes the dealer raised it from $134,995 on November 20 to $149,995 within six days.

The gains are concentrated at the top and middle of the market rather than across all trims. The CarGurus data shows the 2024 model year up 11.68% in 30 days to $91,220 while the 2025 is flat at $80,979 with no change over the same period.

Electrek noted that higher asking prices do not necessarily reflect transaction values and warned that parts and service for a low-volume truck Tesla no longer makes could weigh on used values more than configurator price hikes help them. A top comment from Philip234 argued that asking prices are up but transaction prices would resume cratering, while Electrek cautioned buyers against paying discontinuation hype.
items.title: Used Tesla Cybertruck Prices Jump After Musk Kills It, One Asks $150K

items.summary:
On Friday, Nov. 27, OpenAI filed counterclaims in California federal court against Apple, accusing the company of stealing its trade secrets and blocking access to hardware suppliers after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching employees to gain entry into its technology. The ChatGPT maker argued that Apple's employment practices were designed to 'trap' workers and prevent them from working on competitors' products.

The two companies have not responded to requests for comment from Reuters, though tensions between them are intensifying amid a broader race to develop AI hardware. Earlier this year, Apple brought its initial suit against OpenAI and two former employees, alleging misappropriation of trade secrets tied to the ChatGPT company's move into consumer devices; OpenAI has denied those allegations.

The litigation centers on control over future AI devices that may not rely on traditional apps or operating systems. Analysts suggest such hardware could shift consumer attention away from Apple's iPhone and believe OpenAI is developing a phone or other device of its own.
items.title: OpenAI Countersues Apple Over Alleged Trade Secret Theft

items.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India lowered its minimum daily maintenance requirement for the cash reserve ratio (CRR) from 99% to 90%, effective from the reporting fortnight beginning December 1, 2026. The central bank announced the change in a notification issued on Friday, citing an assessment of current and evolving macroeconomic conditions along with prevailing liquidity situations.

The reduction is intended to give commercial banks wider operational latitude for managing short-term cash mismatches during periods of tight liquidity. Banks will thereby retain more funds outside mandatory reserves, providing additional room to address temporary imbalances in their day-to-day cash positions.
items.title: RBI Lowers Daily CRR Requirement to Ease Bank Cash Crunch

items.summary:
HP has launched the OmniBook Ultra 16 laptop in India, a machine priced at nearly Rs. 5.5 lakh that targets developers and creative professionals rather than casual users seeking video calls or everyday browsing. The device is built around hardware designed to handle artificial intelligence workloads directly on the unit, according to HP's framing of the product. Its stated purpose is to give these professional users the computing resources needed to run compatible AI models, applications, and intelligent agents without relying entirely on cloud-based services.

The launch was accompanied by a separate editorial note pointing readers toward details about upcoming iQOO 16 and iQOO 16s smartphones, including their design and colour options revealed ahead of the December 8 launch. That mention concerns unrelated products and does not describe any feature or specification shared with the HP laptop.
items.title: HP launches OmniBook Ultra 16 in India with NVIDIA RTX Spark

items.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India has decided to restore the minimum daily maintenance norm for its cash reserve ratio (CRR), reducing it from 99 percent back to 90 percent of the requirement, effective from the fortnight beginning December 1, 2026. The central bank cited liquidity tightness in the banking system as the reason for easing the standard that had been tightened two months earlier.

The October step had raised the minimum daily maintenance of CRR from 90 percent to 99 percent effective from the fortnight beginning October 16, 2026. That tightening was necessitated because variable rate reverse repo auctions were not sufficient to offset surplus rupee liquidity generated by a US dollar-rupee forex swap facility RBI provided for fresh foreign currency non-resident deposits mobilised between June 8 and August 31, 2026.

With the latest announcement, RBI has returned CRR maintenance to its prior level within two months. The current overall CRR ratio stands at 3 percent, and resources deployed as CRR do not earn interest. V Rama Chandra Reddy, Head of Treasury at Karur Vysya Bank, described the move as welcome relief that eases day-to-day management and moderates liquidity pressures; he noted banks had kept substantial standing deposit facility balances even under the 99 percent regime due to uneven liquidity distribution, and predicted lower such balances now. K Arvind, Head of Treasury at Tamilnad Mercantile Bank, said the change provides operational flexibility in meeting daily CRR requirements.

Reddy also clarified that the decision will not inject additional liquidity into the banking system but should give banks greater flexibility in managing CRR obligations.
items.title: RBI Restores CRR Maintenance to 90 Percent from December

items.summary:
India's Adani Group is targeting around ₹2.2 lakh crore ($23.72 billion) in capital expenditure for fiscal 2027, according to chief finance officer Jugeshinder Singh speaking at Trust Group's debt capital market summit in Mumbai on Friday.

Singh said the group will invest $10 billion in data centres over the next four years and plans a public issuance of dollar-denominated debt from Adani Ports starting April in the next financial year, with 20-year papers under consideration. The conglomerate had earlier this month announced more than $120 billion in capital expenditure planned across its core infrastructure businesses and emerging growth platforms over five years.

The group set borrowing targets of ₹1.3 lakh crore to ₹1.4 lakh crore each for the current financial year and next, with Singh saying 75% to 80% of borrowings would come from local markets while the remainder is raised globally in coming years. Adani Enterprises will proceed with its fourth public issue in December, and Adani Power is expected to become a larger borrower in the rupee bond market going forward.

The report was published on November 27, 2026.
items.title: Adani Group Plans ₹2.2 Lakh Crore Capex in FY27

items.summary:
WhatsApp announced it will soon let users buy and install a data eSIM for international travel directly within the app, enabling them to keep using WhatsApp on their existing phone number abroad. The Meta-owned company said in a blog post Thursday that it is working with eSIM providers and telecom partners including Jio, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications, and Verizon, though it did not name the countries where the feature would launch or provide pricing details.

In the announcement, WhatsApp described the service as allowing users to purchase and install an eSIM in just a few taps without leaving the app, so travelers can avoid airport kiosks, seek out Wi-Fi cafés, or incur roaming charges. The company framed this effort as part of its early explorations around eSIMs.

WhatsApp Head Kunal Shah characterized the initiative on X as one of the company's early explorations into eSIMs and an invitation to partners worldwide to join what he called 'this important mission.' Meta reported that WhatsApp has more than 3 billion users globally.
items.title: WhatsApp to Sell Travel eSIMs In-App With Jio and Verizon Among Partners
